The bot in the n8n interface: for every workflow an overview and below it one image per module with the section's explanation. Every image can be clicked and then zoomed (mouse wheel, buttons, dragging) — press Esc to close it again. As of: 24 Sep 2026, 11:54.

Where the interface lives

  • Address: https://YOUR-N8N-HOST (in the local network http://192.168.178.53:5678)
  • Seven radio workflows: the agent, three tools, the centre ("Configuration – all values"), "Voices from Films" and the archive (chapters below)
  • Rule: only look in the interface — changes are made in the plan, REPLIKATION/bau/agent-wf-bauen.py

Radio - Telegram Agent0

Voice message (own branch above)

Voice messages get their own branch at the top: fetch the file, download it, turn it into text on the GPU (faster-whisper) and pass the recognised text on. If nothing can be understood, there is a short question back.

Contains: Fetch file, Download audio, Convert, Transcript, Understood?, Heard text

Entry and access

Two entry points (Telegram and Test input) run into the same message preparation. Then Access checks whether the sender is the operator; the short paths answer via Send (short note) without bothering the model.

Contains: Telegram Trigger, Test input, Input, Voice message?, Access, Allowed?, No access, No text, Send (short note), Configuration, Plan switch?

Services: playlists and messages

The service paths in one area: playlists (create, fill, start, delete) and messages (announce, discard). Both run via the radio-tts service; Service reply collects the return value.

Contains: Text present?, Task, Service kind, Service?, Message?, Message service, Playlist service, Service reply, Send failed?, Service fallback send, End, Service send

Inbox (search bot -> moderator)

The inbox: every five minutes the schedule fetches new messages and presents them as a card with buttons. Offer message marks them as offered — no second offer for the same message.

Contains: Schedule messages, Fetch messages, Message present?, Message card, Offer?, Offer message

Stage 0 and stage 1: understand and plan

Stages 0 and 1: first, fixed rules recognise simple commands (song request, skip, status, overview, inbox question) — that costs no model time. Only if nothing fits does the language model plan, and Read commands turns that into the command list.

Contains: Short way?, Shortcut?, Plan, Plan reply, Plan present?, Remember plan, Plan again?, Read commands, Command present?

Stage 2: execution in the loop

Contains: Loop, Execute, Language model execute, Collect result, Fallback tool, Direct or AI?, Controls?, Inbox?, Fetch inbox, Inbox reply, Overview?, Fetch overview, Overview reply, Short controls, Controls reply, Fallback reply

Tools (sub-interfaces of the agent)

The agent's eight tool nodes. Each points to its own workflow (Radio, AzuraCast, Messages) — that keeps the main workflow readable and the tools separately checkable.

Contains: Tool title search, Tool direction search, Tool what's playing, Tool Azura addresses, Tool Azura call, Tool Azura overview, Tool messages, Tool research

Stage 3: check, retry and reply

Contains: Fetch status, Fetch queue, Commands and status, Check?, Check, Check reply, Read check, Retry?, Loop 2, Retry work, Language model retry, Collect follow-up, Build reply, Reply, Send

Tool - Radio0

Switches

The tool's entry: Direction? decides between a mood request, a title search and the pure state.

Contains: Entry, Direction?, Status only?, Configuration

Branch: direction

Direction requests ("something upbeat”, "90s”) go to the catalogue service; the suggestions come back as a selection list.

Contains: Search direction, Prepare suggestions

Branch: title search

The title search asks the catalogue service first (fuzzy, typo tolerant) and then the station's full-text search; Prepare hits merges both lists.

Contains: Smart search, Station search, Prepare hits

Branch: what's playing

The state: current track, what comes next, listener count — prepared as a short text.

Contains: NowPlaying, Prepare status

Playback

The playback path: clear the queue, then insert now or insert after. Exactly one path is taken, depending on the request.

Contains: Hits present?, Queue it?, Clear queue, Insert now, Insert after

Output

The output node: the tool workflow ends here and returns the result to the agent.

Contains: Result

Switches

The entry: look up an address, call an endpoint or give an overview.

Contains: Entry, Look up addresses?, API call?, Configuration

Branch: addresses

The addresses come from the station API description (263 endpoints) — the model never has to guess an address.

Contains: Fetch description, Find addresses

Branch: call

The call: Guard protects against dangerous calls, Read only? separates reading from writing, and a dry run shows what would happen.

Contains: Guard, Execute?, Read only?, Read, Write, Call result, Dry run

Branch: overview

The overview collects mounts, state and playlists with track counts in one text.

Contains: Mounts, State, Playlists, Overview

Voices from Films

in operation · 20 nodes in 3 modules

ModuleNodes
Start2
Search and start0
Wait and report4

Start

The start: the form …/form/YOUR-WEBHOOK-PATH or the webhook accept the series and the job name.

Contains: Form, Fields

Search and start

The search: /finden finds the series or film in the libraries, /extrahieren starts the job on the voices service (port 8890).

Wait and report

Wait and report: the loop asks /job, gives up after 60 minutes (the job keeps running in the container) and sends result or error via Telegram.

Contains: Running?, Wait, Job, Status

Radio - AI Moderator (archive)0

Entries

Three start paths (by hand, form, webhook) run into the same chain.

Contains: Manual, Form, Webhook

Context

What is playing, and what happened last? This is the basis for the moderation text.

Contains: Fields, Now playing, Research

Text and voice

Out of the context comes a speech text (model), which is cleaned and then spoken by Piper.

Contains: Moderation text, Clean text, Voice, File name

Output

Either speak live (interrupts briefly) or upload as a track.

Contains: Mode, Speak live, Upload

Follow-up

After the upload: wait, find the track in the archive, match the request and submit it.

Contains: Wait, Find title, Match, Submit request, Reply

Old helpers

Remains of the first edition — not connected, kept as a reminder.

Contains: Choose hit

Notes and documentation in the interface

Every workflow explains itself: frames with a heading and an explanatory sentence, a note on every node, a documentation note at the top (what the workflow is, how to change and check it, which files describe it) and, for old workflows, a legacy note.

What if something needs to be changed?

Do not click in the interface: layout, frames and notes are created by the builder tool; a click in n8n would be gone with the next import.
